title: Price your jewellery so every sale pays you

say: Price your jewellery so every sale pays you.
This is the video for Module 5 of Advanced Beadwork and Jewellery Making: collections, photography, pricing and custom orders.
Advanced pieces take hours of skilled work.

say: A collection is a small family of pieces that clearly belong together. Give it one theme, two or three colours, one metal tone and one repeated element, like the same resin shape in every piece.

panel.heading: Plan a collection with a price ladder
items: One theme, palette, metal tone, repeated element
Hero: one showstopper for photos
Mid-range: two or three pieces
Entry: quick pieces and easy gifts
Five to ten designs is plenty

say: First, materials, from your receipts: beads, wire, findings, resin, thread and packaging.

panel.heading: What every price must cover
items: Materials from your receipts
Labour: hours × your hourly rate
Overhead: data, transport, electricity
Add a profit markup, e.g. 30 to 50%

say: Second, labour. Hours from your time log, times an hourly rate you would accept from someone else for skilled work.

panel.heading: What every price must cover
items: Materials from your receipts
Labour: hours × your hourly rate
Overhead: data, transport, electricity
Add a profit markup, e.g. 30 to 50%

say: Third, overhead, a percentage for running costs like data, transport and electricity. Many small makers use 10 to 20%.

panel.heading: What every price must cover
items: Materials from your receipts
Labour: hours × your hourly rate
Overhead: data, transport, electricity
Add a profit markup, e.g. 30 to 50%

say: Add those three together and you have your cost price.

panel.heading: What every price must cover
items: Materials from your receipts
Labour: hours × your hourly rate
Overhead: data, transport, electricity
Add a profit markup, e.g. 30 to 50%

say: Then add a profit markup, for example 30 to 50%, and round to a clean figure. That is your retail price.

panel.heading: What every price must cover

say: Here is a worked example with Ifeoma's own figures. A boutique in Lagos offers to sell her cuff on consignment and keep 30% of the selling price.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: Materials come to 5,500 naira. Labour is 8 hours at 1,500 naira, which is 12,000 naira.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: Overhead at 10% is 1,750 naira, so her cost price is 19,250 naira.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: With a 40% markup, she rounds the retail price to 27,000 naira.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: But on consignment she would receive only 70%, which is 18,900 naira. That is 350 naira less than her cost. She would lose money.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: To get her cost plus 20% profit after commission, the retail price must be 33,000 naira. She uses that one price everywhere, so she never undercuts the boutique.

card.title: A peyote cuff and a boutique offer
card.note: Her own figures. Naira prices are approximate.

say: Fake SMS alerts and edited transfer screenshots are common scams. Only release goods when you see the money in your own app. Never share your OTP, PIN or login details with anyone.

panel.rule: Confirm every payment in your own bank or payment app.

say: To remember. Build a collection with a price ladder. Price from materials, labour and overhead, then add profit.
Check your share after any commission. Keep one retail price everywhere. And confirm every payment in your own bank app.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Hero, mid-range and entry pieces in one collection
Cost price = materials + labour + overhead
Check your consignment share covers cost and profit
One retail price across all channels
Never trust an SMS alert or screenshot
